verdict.reasoning: Patient reports diarrhea for the last three days, 6–7 times a day, needing to stay close to the toilet and that it has been affecting day-to-day activities and making work difficult: “diarrhea for the last three days… probably like six or seven times a day… I need to stay close to the toilet… it's been affecting my day-to-day activities… it's been quite difficult [at work].”
Patient describes: “loose and watery stool… No, no blood, yeah, just watery and loose stool.”

Patient reports lower abdominal pain on the left side, crampy, intermittent, and not moving elsewhere: “in my lower abdomen… just to one side… on the left side… it feels like a cramp… it comes and goes… Does the pain move anywhere else…? Patient: ‘no, just maybe my stomach.’” Left lower quadrant is a standard inference from “lower abdomen… left side.”
Patient states: “I vomited at the start of the symptoms but now um I've stopped vomiting.”
Patient reports: “I had a loss of appetite… but I've been able to hold down fluids… just soups, and… light foods. Like smoothies and… liquid foods mainly.”

Patient says: “I haven't had a fever, um, at the moment, but I did notice um a temperature when the symptoms started… I felt, um, just a bit hot.” This supports feeling hot initially and currently afebrile.
Patient explicitly notes: “yeah i feel a bit uh weak and shaky.”
Patient states: “I had takeaway about four days ago… I ate at a Chinese restaurant with friends… one child was vomiting, but they haven't got diarrhea.”
Past medical history: “other than um athsma… everything else is fine.” When asked, “is your asthma well-controlled?” patient replies, “yeah, that's fine… that's under control.”
Patient says: “I use an inhaler… I just, yeah, use an inhaler, and uh that's under control.”
Social history: “I'm an accountant” and later “you live with your wife and two children, is that right? Patient: Yes, yeah.”
Doctor asks: “do you smoke at all?” Patient: “no, I don't smoke.” Then: “do you drink much in the way of alcohol?” Patient: “no, I I don't drink alcohol, no.”

Doctor summarizes: “it seems like you may have something, uh, called gastroenteritis… mainly caused by viruses but there can be a possibility of bacteria… you've been having loose stool, diarrhea… tummy pain mainly on the left-hand side, um and vomiting and fever… you mentioned you had this Chinese takeaway… I wondered whether that might be the cause.” This matches suspected acute gastroenteritis, possibly viral/bacterial, possibly foodborne, with 3 days of watery diarrhea 6–7 times/day, LLQ cramps, initial vomiting now resolved, no blood, and tolerating fluids as previously described.

Doctor advises conservative management and oral rehydration: “what we'd recommend is… conservative management… making sure you're well hydrated, so drinking fluids… there are things like Dioralyte you can get from the pharmacy… it helps replenish your minerals and vitamins.”
Doctor states: “If you are feeling feverish and weak, eh taking some paracetamol, uh, two tablets up to four times a day for the first few days can also help.”

Doctor advises rest and time off: “I will certainly advise you to take some time off work… I would say the next two, two to three days as the infection clears from your system to take some time off and rest.”
Doctor explicitly says: “I don't think you need anything like antibiotics. It's really just… making sure you're well hydrated…” indicating no antibiotics prescribed at this stage.

Follow-up advice: “if your symptoms haven't got better, you know, in in three to four days, I'd like to come and see you again.” This implies follow-up if not improving; worsening is generally encompassed by need for review though not verbatim, but intent aligns.

Doctor notes possible future tests: “if it is ongoing then we have to wonder whether something else caused your symptoms… and we may need to do further tests like um taking a sample of your stool so we can test that.”
